paper.title: Multi-objective Contextual Multi-armed Bandit with a Dominant Objective

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual multi-armed bandit with a dominant objective (CMAB-DO)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Multi-objective (vector-valued, two-dimensional) rewards with lexicographic optimality; out of scope per ontology scope rules.
unmapped: two-dimensional reward vector (dominant and non-dominant objective); optimal arm is lexicographically optimal
contexts in [0,1]^d, arbitrary sequence; expected rewards Hölder continuous in the context with constant L and exponent alpha in (0,1]
the learner knows the Hölder constant L and exponent alpha
regret measured as 2D regret or Pareto regret
settings.definition_quote: At the beginning of round $t$, the learner observes a $d$-dimensional context denoted by $x_t$... the learner selects an arm $a_t$ from a finite set ${\cal A}$, and then, observes a two dimensional random reward $\bs{r}_t = (r^1_t, r^2_t)$... the marginal distribution of $\kappa^i_t$ is conditionally 1-sub-Gaussian

settings.name_in_paper: CMAB-DO with periodically changing reward distributions (extended time context)
unmapped: expected rewards change periodically with known period T_s; Hölder continuous in extended (d+1)-dim context including time
learner knows period T_s, Hölder constant L_hat and exponent alpha_hat
two-dimensional reward vector with dominant objective
settings.definition_quote: let $T_s$ denote the period... $x_{d+1,t} := ( t \mod T_s )/T_s$ is the time context... Assumption 2: $| \mu^{i}_{a}(\hat{x}) - \mu^{i}_{a}(\hat{x}') | \leq \hat{L} || \hat{x}- \hat{x}' ||^{\hat{\alpha}}$

results.notes: Dominant objective; overall O_tilde(T^{(2alpha+d)/(3alpha+d)}). Regret defined through means, so pseudo-regret.

conditions: Assumption 2: expected rewards Hölder continuous in extended context (including periodic time coordinate) with constants L_hat, alpha_hat

source.quote: When MOC-MAB is run with inputs $\hat{L}$, $\hat{\alpha}$, $m = \lceil T^{1/(3\hat{\alpha}+d+1)} \rceil$, and $\beta >0$ by using the extended context set $\hat{{\cal X}}$ instead of the original context set ${\cal X}$, we have $\expect{ \text{Reg}^i(T) } = \tilde{O} ( T^{(2 \hat{\alpha} + d + 1)/(3 \hat{\alpha} + d + 1)}  ) \text{ for } i \in \{1,2\}$

results.notes: Applies to both objectives i=1,2. Environment mapping (periodic changes) to nonstationary_drifting is approximate.
